failed_calls_retries.assessment: The committed session made 123 tool calls and had 1 failed call, a failure rate of approximately 0.81%. The lone failure was a reroute geometry validation error at turn 114; the next call changed the endpoint configuration rather than repeating the invalid corners, and no error class recurred. There were no rejected finalize or resolve_request calls. The recorded retry belongs to an invalid-infrastructure attempt and is excluded from scoring.

lint_etiquette.assessment: The transcript contains approximately 29 error-severity lint firings, concentrated in covered-content conflicts while routing greeting and policy-loop edges. The agent repeatedly changed tactics—moving labels, shortening or removing labels, shifting segments, and rerouting—and ultimately reached clean diagnostics. Because the strategy changed during the prolonged sequence, it does not meet the strict definition of the same lint re-fired for more than three consecutive turns with no strategy change. No warning was committed via override, so neither reasoned nor silent warning overrides apply.

commit_honesty.assessment: There was one commit. Its summary is broadly supported by the stage diff: ANI lookup and greeting branches, consent and speech/keypad intent capture, AI account-fact lookup and authorized actions, human queue with transfer-package note and callback branch, and the review-to-policy-to-AI loop are all present. The word "complete" is somewhat broad, but the concrete listed components match the diff and clean final render closely enough that it is not counted as an inflated claim. No defect seen by the agent remained undeclared at commit.

economy.assessment: The committed session produced 46 final patch operations but used 123 tool calls over 23.37 minutes, exceeding the 15-minute session budget. It also contained one explicit add-then-delete cycle: the intent fallback edge was added at turn 93 and deleted at turn 94. The long series of greeting-label and policy-edge route adjustments was costly, though it ultimately converged rather than being abandoned. One NO-OP occurred at turn 64 and was not repeated, so it is not NO-OP thrash.
